disease: Autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa, RHO-related (adRP; RHO toxic gain-of-function / rhodopsin misfolding, e.g. P23H)

emergence.disease: Autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa, RHO-related (adRP; RHO toxic gain-of-function / rhodopsin misfolding, e.g. P23H)
emergence.summary: Autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa (adRP) is the dominantly-inherited form of the commonest inherited retinal dystrophy, and RHO -- the gene encoding rhodopsin, the light-sensing G-protein-coupled receptor of the rod photoreceptor outer segment (chr3q22.1) -- is its single commonest cause (~20-30% of adRP). More than 200 RHO alleles are known; the disease is mechanistically heterogeneous, but the dominant, classic and most-studied class is a TOXIC GAIN-of-function (class II), epitomised by P23H: the mutant opsin MISFOLDS, is retained in the endoplasmic reticulum, overwhelms proteostasis and exerts a dominant-negative / cytotoxic aggregation gain on the rod, driving progressive rod-then-cone death and concentric visual-field loss. The kit reads this with the PROTEINOPATHY pattern it already uses for Huntington (HTT), transthyretin amyloidosis (TTR) and SOD1-ALS: the toxic misfolded species acts as an OVER-ACTIVE pathological BRAKE suppressing photoreceptor homeostasis (role brake, mechanism GOF -> emergent axis DOWN on photoreceptor maintenance throughput), the burden to be REMOVED rather than a lost function to be supplied. Correction is therefore to REDUCE the toxic mutant rhodopsin: mutation-specific knockdown of the mutant allele -- e.g. the P23H-directed antisense oligonucleotide QR-1123 (which lowers toxic mutant-protein accumulation and reached a Phase 1/2 trial), allele-specific CRISPR/RNAi -- and mutation-agnostic 'ablate-and-replace' (knock down endogenous RHO and supply a resistant wild-type copy, e.g. the dual-AAV EDIT-103, preclinical) all push the toxic-species axis the corrective way (reduce the poison). HONESTLY: there is NO approved drug or gene therapy for RHO-adRP anywhere; the lead corrective agents are clinical-not-approved or preclinical, so the kit ships this in the SAME honest shape as Huntington, X-linked RP and choroideremia (DNA readable, lead lever NOT a clean approved switch-drug; direction [F], magnitude [O]) -- the Huntington pattern, now its FOURTH instance. This is the kit's FOURTH ocular read and its FIRST ocular PROTEINOPATHY: where LCA2 (RPE65) is a retinoid-CYCLE ENZYME deficiency, X-linked RP (RPGR) is a ciliary-TRAFFICKING deficiency and choroideremia (CHM/REP1) is a Rab-PRENYLATION deficiency -- three LOSS reads on three different retinal machines -- RHO-adRP is the FIRST ocular read whose lesion is a toxic GAIN (a misfolded protein), and the FIRST ocular AUTOSOMAL-DOMINANT read (the prior three are recessive or X-linked). It also sharpens a within-kit contrast: rhodopsin is literally a light-sensing GPCR, so RHO-adRP is a GPCR-GENE read carried as a proteinopathy, the toxic-GAIN counterpart to the same release's AVPR2 nephrogenic-DI read (a signalling-GPCR LOSS). Mechanistic heterogeneity is recorded honestly: a MINORITY of RHO adRP alleles act by LOF / haploinsufficiency (class I null / dominant-negative), for which the toxic-reduce read does not apply -- so the read is clean for the toxic-GOF majority but allele-contested (direction_confidence cited-contested). The gamma read is of the RHO promoter switch STRUCTURE (chr3q22.1); the disease lesions (P23H and the other >200 coding alleles) are coding, outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
emergence.emergent_axis: rod photoreceptor outer-segment maintenance / proteostatic throughput -- a toxic misfolded rhodopsin species (the P23H class-II majority) acts as an over-active pathological brake on photoreceptor homeostasis, the maintenance axis pushed DOWN (the proteinopathy pattern: HTT, TTR, SOD1 -> remove the toxic species). The kit's first ocular proteinopathy and first toxic-GAIN ocular read, the gain contrast to the three loss-of-function ocular reads (RPE65 enzyme, RPGR cilia, CHM Rab-prenylation)

per_gene.note: RHO encodes rhodopsin, the rod photoreceptor light-sensing GPCR. The classic dominant adRP class (II) is a TOXIC gain-of-function: P23H (and many other) mutant opsins misfold, are ER-retained and exert a dominant-negative/cytotoxic aggregation gain on the rod -> progressive photoreceptor death. Read with the HTT/TTR/SOD1 proteinopathy convention as an over-active pathological brake on photoreceptor homeostasis (brake/GOF -> axis DOWN; the toxic species to REDUCE). chr3q22.1. NCBI official symbol RHO. RP4 (adRP) = OMIM 613731. Coding lesions; promoter firewall respected. A minority of RHO adRP alleles are instead LOF (class I) -- noted, not folded into this toxic-GOF read.

treatment_A_switch.disease: Autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa, RHO-related (adRP; RHO toxic gain-of-function / rhodopsin misfolding, e.g. P23H)

levers.push_direction: lower the toxic misfolded mutant rhodopsin (allele-specific knockdown of the mutant transcript) -> relieve the proteostatic burden on the rod -> raise photoreceptor maintenance throughput back toward normal (reduce the toxic species, the HTT/TTR/SOD1 corrective direction)
levers.agent_class: mutation-specific mutant-allele knockdown -- antisense oligonucleotide (QR-1123, targeting P23H; reached Phase 1/2) / allele-specific CRISPR / RNAi
levers.mechanism_grade: [O] the degree of toxic-protein lowering and the photoreceptor-rescue MAGNITUDE are not sequence-derived; allele-specific knockdown applies to the toxic-GOF class only (class I LOF alleles are not addressed by it); NO agent is approved for RHO-adRP -- the corrective DIRECTION (reduce the toxic mutant) is forced [F]
levers.src: Murray 2015 Mol Ther Nucleic Acids 4:e258 (P23H allele-specific knockdown); ProQR QR-1123 (P23H ASO, Phase 1/2, NCT04123626); Cideciyan 2018 (allele-specific approaches in adRP)

levers.push_direction: mutation-agnostic 'ablate-and-replace': knock down endogenous RHO and supply a knockdown-resistant wild-type RHO copy -> remove the toxic mutant AND restore functional rhodopsin (covers many RHO alleles with one construct)
levers.mechanism_grade: [O] efficiency of mutant ablation, wild-type replacement level and rescue magnitude not derived; preclinical, not approved; direction [F]
levers.src: Cideciyan 2018 PNAS 115:E8547 (mutation-independent knockdown-and-replace for RHO adRP); EDIT-103 (Editas/dual-AAV, preclinical)

falsifiers.claim: the toxic-GOF RHO allele (P23H class) moves the photoreceptor-maintenance axis DOWN (an over-active toxic brake)
falsifiers.falsifier: a P23H-class RHO allele that IMPROVED photoreceptor survival / outer-segment proteostasis, or in which the misfolded opsin raised rather than suppressed rod maintenance, would refute the toxic-brake (axis DOWN) read
falsifiers.measurable_by: rod survival / outer-segment integrity (ONL thickness, ERG a-wave) in a P23H RHO knock-in retina; photoreceptor proteostatic-stress markers by genotype

falsifiers.claim: REDUCING the toxic mutant rhodopsin (allele-specific knockdown) is the CORRECTIVE direction
falsifiers.falsifier: if lowering the mutant RHO transcript ACCELERATED photoreceptor degeneration in toxic-GOF adRP, the reduce-the-toxin lever sign is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: photoreceptor survival / ERG response to allele-specific RHO knockdown in a P23H adRP retina
